title: A decision removes future choices only at the right level; out of context it is noise (2026-10-28)

sections.name: narrative
sections.label: Narrative
sections.content:
We also need to see when decisions appear in the wrong context.

If we define a decision as a choice that removes future choices then it only does that at the right level. 

A technical adr in a strategy context does not remove any options. But when seen at a technical level, it's impact may be huge.

Decisions are relevant in the domains where they are relevant. If we don't have the domains defined at the right levels, then our decisions just become noise.
